name: Treasury Building, Brisbane
scope: The four-front former Treasury Building as it stood in 2005, with the sandstone street walls, corner pavilions and covered central courtyard from the 1990s adaptation. The separate former Land Administration Building, its hotel, and interiors are outside this model.

references.filename: StateLibQld 1 139704 Lord Lamington addresses Federation Day crowds, Brisbane, 1901.jpg

originalReview.notes: Contemporary 1901 image confirms the surviving William Street classical arcades, projecting pavilions and upper parapets. Its crowds, temporary festival decoration and the earlier setting are excluded.

Full Elizabeth Street elevation identifies the warm sandstone, paired arched windows, regular cornice courses, taller corner pavilions and entry placement. It was originally published in November 2005.

review.method: Two exact Qualla originals with creator and institutional public-domain records
review.notes: Qualla checked first. Figaro’s exact originally published exterior has a first-person public-domain release preserved by Commons. The exact 1901 State Library of Queensland original was transferred by the institutional bot as public domain, with the original object record at https://collections.slq.qld.gov.au/viewer/IE53437. Its photograph was used only for the surviving William Street fabric. The colored postcard shows the incomplete Queen Street frontage and was excluded.
